newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM says will form centre-right cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM says will form centre-right cabinet.

text.p: Slovenian prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek said he wanted to name a new cabinet on Monday that would comprise ministers from his own Liberal Democrats (LDS) and the conservative People's Party (SLS).
It will be Drnovsek's second and final attempt at forming a government since an inconclusive general election in November. Parliament voted down his first, leftist cabinet 10 days ago.

"The first coalition and cabinet line-up had no guarantee of success this time around. Therefore, the council of the LDS agreed in principle on a coalition with the SLS, with the support of (pensioners' party) Desus," Drnovsek told Radio Slovenia late on Sunday.
Sources close to Drnovsek said the cabinet announcement was expected on Monday afternoon.

SLS, which has 19 seats in the 90-seat parliament and is the second largest parliamentary group after Drnovsek's centre-left LDS, confirmed the coalition agreement but said negotiations were not over yet.
"The main board of SLS has accepted the proposal of the executive board that SLS forms a government coalition with LDS," People's Party head Marjan Podobnik told the radio.
He forecast the LDS would gain 10 ministerial posts while the SLS would take nine portfolios.
The two parties, which together hold 44 parliamentary seats, may also invite pensioners' party Desus to join the government. It has five seats and could gain one ministerial position.
Analysts said Drnovsek's latest team stood a good chance of winning parliamentary approval.

"According to the statements of the two parties, it seems nothing could go wrong now as the new coalition, which has a very good chances of gaining sufficient parliamentary support, seems to be agreed upon," one political analyst said.
Drnovsek first tried to form a government with the former communists the United List of Social Democrats, Desus and the Nationalist Party.
If parliament fails to comfirm at least two thirds of the second line-up, President Milan Kucan will have to nominate a new prime minister.
Drnovsek has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
The new government would be the third after Slovenia's independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
